newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Harris Scarfe half sales up 15.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Harris Scarfe half sales up 15.6 pct.

text.p: Retail group Harris Scarfe Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday its sales rose by 15.6 percent to A$123.65 million in the first half of the 1996/97 financial year compared to the previous year.
"The 'like for like' increase in the first half was a satisfactory 4.2 percent," the company said in a statement.
Managing director Ron Baker said the increase in sales had not been easy to achieve and some pre-Christmas discounting was needed to achieve the sales budgets.
"This has led to some reduction in the gross profit rate across the business," he said.
"However because of the low cost structure of Harris Scarfe we expect a very satisfactory profit result for the first half," he said, adding that results were due in the first week of March.

Baker said the company was well-placed to continue its growth in sales and profitability in the second half, although he expected this period to be as tough as any he had experienced in his 30 years of retailing.

"With our mix of merchandise being skewed away from fashion areas, we should continue to grow the business in other areas such as homewares, which has been very strong for the company in the first half," he said.
Chairman Donald Trescowthick said the board was delighted with the company's sales performance in a very difficult and competitive retail market.
The 'like for like' growth compared well to the performance of competitors and the current low inflationary environment, he said.

Baker said the acquisition in November of the Stirlings chain in rural Western Australia had been a real success for the company: the three stores had been re-badged and were all trading well ahead of budgets and their previous performance.
Further expansion in the WA market was expected by the company, with a 4,000 square metre store to open in Cottesloe next month, and Victorian expansion continuing, he said.
